Week 2 — Setting Up Python and Working with Real Data

Week 2 — Setting Up Python, Google Colab, VS Code, and Your First Dataset

Week 1 removed fear.

Week 2 builds computational independence.

This week focuses on:

  • computational environments
  • cloud vs local computing
  • Google Colab
  • VS Code
  • datasets
  • CSV files
  • loading real-world data into Python

This week is foundational.

If students fail here, everything later becomes difficult.

1. Learning Objectives

By the end of this week, students should be able to:

  • explain what a computational environment is
  • distinguish between cloud and local computing
  • use Google Colab effectively
  • understand the role of VS Code
  • upload datasets
  • read CSV files using Python
  • inspect a real-world dataset using pandas

2. What Is a Computational Environment?

A computational environment is the workspace where we write and run code.

Examples include:

Environment Description
Google Colab Cloud-based notebook environment
Jupyter Notebook Local notebook environment
VS Code Professional coding environment
Spyder Scientific Python IDE
RStudio IDE mainly used for R

In this course, we mainly use:

  • Google Colab
  • VS Code
  • GitHub

3. Cloud vs Local Computing

There are two major ways to run Python.

Option 1 — Cloud Computing

Example:

Google Colab

Advantages:

  • no installation required
  • works on most computers
  • easy sharing
  • ideal for beginners
  • free access to computing resources

Disadvantages:

  • requires internet connection
  • temporary session storage

Option 2 — Local Computing

Example:

VS Code + Local Python Installation

Advantages:

  • works offline
  • faster for large projects
  • professional workflow
  • better file control

Disadvantages:

  • installation required
  • more technical setup issues

Course Recommendation

Tool Purpose
Google Colab Main classroom environment
VS Code Long-term development environment
GitHub Storing and sharing work

Install VS Code.

7. Installing Python

Python itself must be installed separately for local work.

Download Python from:

https://python.org

Important Installation Step

During installation, check:

Add Python to PATH

This is extremely important.

Verify Installation

Open terminal and run:

python --version

You should see something like:

Python 3.12

8. Installing Required Libraries

Libraries are collections of tools created by other programmers.

We use libraries instead of building everything from scratch.

Important Libraries for This Course

Library Purpose
pandas Data handling
numpy Numerical calculations
matplotlib Graphs
plotly Interactive visualization
scikit-learn Machine learning
statsmodels Econometrics

Installation Command

Run this in terminal:

pip install pandas numpy matplotlib plotly scikit-learn statsmodels

9. Understanding Files and Folders

Good organization is essential.

Bad file management destroys projects.

Recommended Folder Structure

Industrial_Data_Analytics/
│
├── datasets/
├── notebooks/
├── assignments/
├── outputs/
└── drafts/

Naming Conventions

Good:

inflation_data_2025.csv

Bad:

datafinalfinal2.csv

Students must learn discipline early.

10. What Is a Dataset?

A dataset is a structured collection of information.

Datasets contain:

  • rows
  • columns
  • variables
  • observations

Example Dataset

Year Inflation GDP Growth
2020 4.6 -3.6
2021 6.0 3.7
2022 46.4 -7.8

Important Terminology

Term Meaning
Row One observation
Column One variable
Observation One unit of data
Variable Measured characteristic

11. What Is a CSV File?

CSV stands for:

Comma-Separated Values

CSV files are one of the most common formats in economics and data science.

Example:

Year,Inflation,GDP_Growth
2020,4.6,-3.6
2021,6.0,3.7

Why CSV Files Matter

CSV files:

  • are lightweight
  • work across software
  • are easy to import
  • are widely used

12. Your First Real Dataset

This week we use a simple Sri Lankan macroeconomic dataset.

Variables include:

  • year
  • inflation
  • GDP growth
  • unemployment
  • exchange rate

Example Table

Year Inflation GDP_Growth Exchange_Rate
2020 4.6 -3.6 185
2021 6.0 3.7 200
2022 46.4 -7.8 360

13. Reading Data Using Pandas

We use the pandas library to work with datasets.

Import Pandas

import pandas as pd

Read CSV File

data = pd.read_csv("sri_lanka_macro.csv")

Display First Rows

data.head()

head() shows the first few rows of the dataset.

Display Dataset Information

data.info()

This shows:

  • number of rows
  • columns
  • variable types
  • missing values

Summary Statistics

data.describe()

This calculates:

  • mean
  • standard deviation
  • minimum
  • maximum
  • quartiles

14. Understanding Data Types

Python stores different kinds of information differently.

Common Data Types

Type Example
Integer 5
Float 5.2
String “Sri Lanka”
Boolean True

Example

inflation = 46.4
country = "Sri Lanka"

19. Mini Quiz

Question 1

What does CSV stand for?

A. Central Statistical Variable
B. Comma-Separated Values
C. Computer Statistical Verification
D. Column Sorted Values

Correct answer: B

Question 2

Which library is mainly used for data handling?

A. matplotlib
B. numpy
C. pandas
D. sklearn

Correct answer: C

Question 3

What does head() do?

A. Deletes rows
B. Creates graphs
C. Displays first rows
D. Saves dataset

Correct answer: C

Question 4

Which command imports pandas?

import pandas as pd
load pandas
pandas.open()
import data

Correct answer: A

22. Common Errors

Problem 1 — File Not Found

Error:

FileNotFoundError

Possible causes:

  • dataset not uploaded
  • wrong filename

Problem 2 — Forgetting Quotes

Wrong:

pd.read_csv(sri_lanka_macro.csv)

Correct:

pd.read_csv("sri_lanka_macro.csv")

Problem 3 — Forgetting Import Statement

Wrong:

data = pd.read_csv("file.csv")

without importing pandas first.

Correct:

import pandas as pd

Problem 4 — Wrong File Path

If dataset is inside another folder:

pd.read_csv("datasets/sri_lanka_macro.csv")

23. AI Reflection Question

AI tools can summarize datasets and generate code.

However:

  • AI can misunderstand datasets
  • AI may generate incorrect code
  • AI can produce weak interpretations

Reflection question:

Why is human interpretation still necessary even when AI tools can analyze data?

24. Key Takeaways

By the end of Week 2, students should understand:

  • the difference between cloud and local computing
  • how to use Google Colab
  • how to use VS Code
  • how datasets are structured
  • how CSV files work
  • how to import datasets using pandas
  • how to inspect real-world data
